name: Federal Bank Ltd
title: Federal Bank Ltd - 500469 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Federal Bank Q4 FY26 shows record profit of INR1,145 cr and ROA back to pre-rate-cut levels, but about INR456 cr one-off tax-refund interest flatters reported numbers and ECL transition is unquantified.

triggers.label: One-off tax refund gains flatter Q4
triggers.quote: the numbers I'm going to spell out are on the underlying performance metrics, which will be detailing our core earnings trajectory, excluding impact of one-off gains

triggers.label: Credit cost guidance held pending ECL
triggers.quote: we don't want to review our guidance for now

red_flags.label: One-off tax refund interest flatters profit
red_flags.quote: the INR456 crores number that you see in our -- as a one-off

red_flags.label: Floating provision of INR456 cr for ECL
red_flags.quote: floating provision has nothing whatsoever to do with asset quality

red_flags.label: Falling LCR buffer
red_flags.quote: we are currently operating at about 120% roughly

evasions.quote: Let me leave the guidance at that.
We don't want to quantify that
We will come back to you on this.

summary.headline: Federal Bank posted record quarterly net profit of INR 1,145 crore (up ~10% QoQ) in Q4 FY26, with CASA crossing INR 1 lakh crore and GNPA at a decade-low 1.62%.
summary.overview: Federal Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR 1,145 crore, its highest ever quarterly profit, on underlying metrics excluding one-off gains. Growth was led by commercial banking, gold, LAP and CV/CE, while CASA and NRE deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore each. Asset quality hit decade-best levels, and a one-time INR 456 crore interest gain from an income tax refund was used partly to build a floating provision ahead of ECL transition. Management declined to revise its credit cost, growth or cost-to-income guidance, and said the ECL impact is still being assessed.

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% QoQ and ~26% YoY, described as primary growth engine.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Grew 9% QoQ and 26% YoY, despite downsizing a sub-segment for regulatory alignment; around 14% of advances, LTV below 54%.

segments.name: LAP
segments.commentary: Expanded 8% QoQ; management expects growth to accelerate.

segments.name: Agriculture and microfinance
segments.commentary: Agriculture grew 5% QoQ; microfinance grew 7.28% QoQ, restarted in small way last quarter.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Grew ~6% YoY; deliberately calibrated to protect yield and portfolio health.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional banking
segments.commentary: Essentially flat QoQ; deliberate credit selectivity toward high-rated counterparties.

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Growing ~23% YoY; growth skewed to transactors rather than revolvers.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost guidance of 50-60 bps retained, not revised; FY26 credit cost was about 56 bps; management said it will reassess once ECL impact and West Asia situation are clearer.
Cost-to-income guidance range of 53%-56% retained; management said it has done slightly better than guidance in FY26.
Further deposit repricing benefit expected in Q1 and early Q2 FY27; NIM expansion expected from mix, not only repricing.
About 100 branches planned for next year after 39 added in Q4 FY26.
Medium-term CASA ratio target of 36% reiterated as achievable; no numeric loan growth guidance given.
ECL transition impact still being assessed; draft guidance indicates the floating provision can be used during transition.
capex_capacity: 39 new branches added in Q4 FY26; slower branch addition in H1 FY26 due to network study and rebranding.
About 100 branch additions planned for FY27.
Branch network restructuring and relocation to improve productivity of existing branches.
Wealth management business launched during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Retail home loans: unattractive pricing (15-year at ~7.15%); bank not pushing volume, which weighs on overall retail growth; retail book flat YoY.
Wholesale deposits reduced during the year; retail term deposits growing faster than system.
Remittances remain elevated; management sees no change unless significant job losses in UAE.
Corporate: targeting early double-digit growth, focus on mid-market (about 75% of NTB acquisitions) and cross-sell.
Competition described as intense and sometimes irrational in rate-setting.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on loan and deposit growth after balance sheet realignment; staff cost decline and one-time provisions treatment.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CASA and retail term deposit growth exceed system and wholesale deposits fell; no numeric FY27 guidance, only said traction is building. Staff cost impact not quantified. Floating provision is for ECL transition and not linked to any specific asset.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and whether deposit repricing is done.
qa_highlights.answer: Some deposit repricing left into Q1 and early Q2 FY27. NIM down only about 2 bps over FY26 on full-year basis. Day count impact present in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and ECL impact on provisions and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East asset exposure described as not large. ECL impact still being assessed; the guidance of 50-60 bps is under reassessment, not yet changed. Current plans unchanged despite West Asia situation.

qa_highlights.question: LCR level and comfort range.
qa_highlights.answer: LCR at 119%; comfortable at 115-120%, down from 135-140% earlier, which management called a NIM drag.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan LTV and pricing practice.
qa_highlights.answer: Gold valued at lower of 30-day average and prior-day price; margins raised during March volatility; LTV below 54%. No internal cap; will reassess if gold loans approach 20% of book.

qa_highlights.question: Credit card and transactor growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Card book grew about 23% YoY, with transactor growth stronger than revolvers as organic cards go mostly to existing customers.

risks_watch: ECL transition: impact not yet quantified; management said it is still early, and draft guidance may change.
West Asia conflict: possible inflation pass-through from Q1 FY27 and potential remittance or NRI-related stress if job losses occur in the Gulf.
Food inflation rose to 3.87% by March, to be monitored into Q1 FY27.
Falling LCR (119%) may constrain CASA growth if the bank pushes it further; LCR fell about 20 points YoY.
Home loan book drag on retail growth; management says it will not chase pricing at current levels.
One-time INR 456 crore interest gain and INR 115 crore tax reversal inflate reported ROA (1.36% vs 1.24% underlying).
summary.management_tone: Confident on liabilities, asset-quality and margin execution, with repeated emphasis on underlying (ex one-off) numbers. Cautious on forward growth and ECL: guidance on credit cost and cost-to-income was left unchanged, and the ECL impact was deferred, citing uncertainty from the West Asia situation.
key_quotes: We delivered INR1,145 crores in net profit, representing nearly 10% sequential growth. Now this is the highest ever quarterly net profit for the bank.
Our NIM story is about multiple levers being pulled, and we are confident that we'll continue to remain agile and build that NIM expansion from here.
This is primarily as a transition to ECL.
Higher LCR than required is also a NIM destroyer.

adds.what: About 100 new bank branches planned for FY27 (after 39 added in Q4 FY26)

growth.why: Management held credit cost (50-60 bps), cost-to-income (53-56%) and gave no numeric loan growth guidance; ~100 branch additions planned for FY27 and deposit repricing/mix expected to support NIM, but no concrete loan-growth targets or orders quantify the outlook.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 3.20% (+2 bps QoQ) with further deposit repricing benefit still to come in Q1 and early Q2 FY27, plus mix-led expansion; cost of deposits already down 5 bps QoQ to 5.43%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 100 branch additions planned for FY27 after 39 added in Q4 FY26, a concrete branch plan, though no plant or capacity-type capex is discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross advances grew 3.65% QoQ and ~13% YoY to INR 2,68,369 crore, with CV/CE up 8.5% QoQ and LAP up 8% QoQ, but no numeric loan growth guidance was given and retail home loans are flat YoY because the bank is not chasing pricing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation are not discussed; the branch rollout is the only expansion and is already in the plan, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management retained credit cost (50-60 bps), cost-to-income (53-56%) and gave no numeric loan growth guidance, and said FY26 cost-to-income was only slightly better than guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost guidance of 50-60 bps is under reassessment for ECL transition and West Asia risk (FY26 credit cost ~56 bps), while LCR fell from 135-140% to 119%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wealth management business was launched in Q4 FY26, but no further product launches or timelines were disclosed.

rows.label: ECL transition impact
rows.why: Impact is still being assessed; draft guidance allows the INR 456 crore-linked floating provision to be used during transition, but the quantum is not yet known.

rows.label: Retail home loan pricing and retail growth drag
rows.why: Retail home loans priced at about 7.15% (15-year) are unattractive, the retail book is flat YoY, and management says it will not chase volume at current levels.

rows.label: Asset quality at decade best
rows.why: GNPA at a decade-low 1.62% and NNPA at an all-time low 0.37% with provision coverage up 141 bps QoQ to 76.55%, supporting credit cost stability.

tone.note: Management was confident on CASA (up 8.26% QoQ to INR 1,03,390 crore), NIM and asset quality, but cautious on forward growth and ECL, leaving credit cost and cost-to-income guidance unchanged; analysts pushed on margin outlook, LCR decline, gold loan LTV and Middle East exposure.
